answer: Cross-epoch intent drift scoring. Each identity’s action distribution (topics, timestamps, counterparties) is hashed per epoch; a consistency signal is the cosine similarity against its prior-epoch centroid. Identities below a 0.7 ridge lose queue priority and rewards. Attackers must maintain coherent, non-farming behavior across epochs, while splitting identities multiplies the nectar cost of sustained plausible activity per fake—forcing sybils to pay for realistic histories they cannot cheaply share.
